summary: EASA sorts aviation activity three ways: commercial or non-commercial, air transport or specialised operation, and complex or other-than-complex aircraft. An aircraft is complex if it meets criteria on mass, seating, crew or engines. The Basic Regulation splits into Part-NCO, Part-FCL and SERA. Modern Part-21 aircraft use these, while non-Part-21 aircraft (microlights, gyroplanes, vintage, ex-military and amateur-built) come under ANO 2016.
sections: EASA classifies civil aviation activity
Commercial or non-commercial, based on the presence of remuneration
Air transport or specialised operation, based on the activity performed
Complex motor-powered or other-than-complex motor-powered, based on the aircraft used
Definition of complex (air operations)
Maximum certificated take-off mass exceeding 5,700 kg
Certificated for a maximum passenger seating configuration of more than 19
Certificated for a minimum crew of at least 2 pilots
Equipped with at least one turbojet engine or more than one turboprop engine
Structure of the assimilated EU law
The Basic Regulation branches into parts for different aspects of aviation
Part-NCO deals with NCO operations
Part-FCL deals with flight crew licensing
SERA (Standardised European Rules of the Air) deals with rules of the air
Documents for a UK pilot in a G-registered aeroplane

ANO 2016: enacted by parliament, with safety requirements for all aircraft in UK airspace and persons involved in aircraft operations; airworthiness, operational and flight crew regulations for non-Part-21 aircraft
UK rules of the air regulations 2015 (SERA UK): all aircraft in UK airspace must adhere
Part-FCL: licensing requirements for Part-21 aeroplanes
Part-NCO: operational regulations for Part-21 other-than-complex motor-powered aircraft
ANO 2016 Part 6 & Schedule 8: licensing for non-Part-21 aircraft
ANO 2016 Part 5 & Schedule 5: operational regulations for non-Part-21 aircraft
Part-21 or non-Part-21?
Most modern factory-built aircraft (not microlights or gyroplanes) are Part-21
Vintage, ex-military, amateur-built aircraft, microlights and gyroplanes are non-Part-21

sum.EASA classifies civil aviation activity: Activity is classified three ways: by payment, by type of operation and by aircraft category.
sum.Definition of complex (air operations): Four tests (mass, seats, crew, engines); meeting any one makes an aircraft complex.
sum.Structure of the assimilated EU law: The Basic Regulation splits into Part-NCO (operations), Part-FCL (licensing) and SERA (rules of the air).
sum.Documents for a UK pilot in a G-register: Which document applies depends on Part-21 status: Part-FCL and Part-NCO for Part-21 aircraft, ANO 2016 for the rest, with UK SERA for everyone.
sum.Part-21 or non-Part-21?: Modern factory-built aircraft are Part-21; microlights, gyroplanes, vintage, ex-military and amateur-built are not.

cards.q: What three ways does EASA classify civil aviation activity?
cards.a: Commercial vs non-commercial; air transport vs specialised operation; complex vs other-than-complex motor-powered aircraft.

cards.q: What decides air transport vs specialised operation?

cards.a: Maximum certificated take-off mass exceeding 5,700 kg.
Maximum certificated seating of more than 19.
At least one turbojet, or more than one turboprop.
Operational regulations for Part-21 other-than-complex motor-powered aircraft.

cards.q: What does SERA stand for, and cover?
cards.a: Standardised European Rules of the Air; the rules of the air.

cards.q: What does the Air Navigation Order (ANO) 2016 contain?
cards.a: Safety requirements for all aircraft in UK airspace and people involved in operating them, including airworthiness, operational and flight crew rules for non-Part-21 aircraft.

cards.q: Which ANO 2016 parts cover licensing and operations for non-Part-21 aircraft?
cards.a: Licensing: Part 6 and Schedule 8. Operations: Part 5 and Schedule 5.
Vintage, ex-military, amateur-built aircraft, microlights and gyroplanes.
Most modern factory-built aircraft, excluding microlights and gyroplanes.

quiz.q: Which take-off mass makes an aircraft complex?
quiz.why: The threshold is a maximum certificated take-off mass exceeding 5,700 kg.

quiz.q: Which maximum seating configuration meets the complex threshold?
quiz.why: More than 19, so exactly 19 does not qualify.
Commercial vs non-commercial depends on the presence of remuneration.

quiz.q: Which engine fit meets the complex criterion?
quiz.why: One turbojet is enough; turboprops need to be more than one.

quiz.q: What separates air transport from specialised operation?
quiz.why: It is based on the activity performed.

quiz.q: Which regulation covers the rules of the air?
quiz.why: SERA is the Standardised European Rules of the Air.

quiz.q: Which part covers flight crew licensing for Part-21 aeroplanes?
Which of these is a non-Part-21 aircraft?
quiz.why: Microlights, gyroplanes, vintage, ex-military and amateur-built aircraft are non-Part-21.

quiz.q: Which part covers operations of Part-21 other-than-complex aircraft?
quiz.why: Part-NCO holds the operational regulations for these aircraft.
